title: Problem type
description: The frontmatter of one problem type file in an error catalogue. Each file documents a single RFC 9457 problem type. The type URI is the catalogue's base_url followed by the slug.

type.description: The slug. Appended to base_url to form the type URI, and must match the filename without .md.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary. It should not change from occurrence to occurrence of the problem.

status.description: The HTTP status code generated by the origin server for this problem.

since.description: The version the type was introduced in.

template.description: The name of the template the type was created from. Its declared extensions must stay present.

extends.description: The absolute URI of a shared problem type this one builds on.

extensions.description: Extension members carried by this problem type, keyed by member name. Each describes the member's value, and nested values can be described with items and properties.

deprecated.description: Present when the type should no longer be used. The type and its URI remain valid.

memberName.description: RFC 9457 section 3.2: starts with a letter, then letters, digits or underscores, at least three characters. The standard members cannot be reused.

propertyName.description: The name of a property inside an object member: starts with a letter, then letters, digits or underscores.

shapeBody.description: What a value looks like. items describes each element of an array, and properties the members of an object; each is only allowed with the matching type.

type.description: The JSON type of the value.

member.description: A named member: an extension, or a property of an object.

required.description: True when the member is always present. Making a required member optional is a breaking change.

since.description: The version the type was deprecated in.

replaced_by.description: The slug of the type to use instead. It must exist in the catalogue and not itself be deprecated.
